Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the City webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, Amazon Fire, iOS and
Android devices using a free app called Cablecast and choosing "Glendale TV" from the menu.
Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas.
Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the
meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that
agenda item is discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for
assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. The City Clerk’ office should be notified 72 hours (three
business days) or as soon as practicable for requests regarding sign language translation and
Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are
received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review
in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting or as soon as
practicable. Please specify the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City
provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak
in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Kassakhian asked council to adjourn in memory of Thomas Jefferson “TJ”
  Benton V. Councilmember Devine spoke fondly of the deceased and sent her condolences to
  the family. Kassakhian asked staff to look into the A Frame Sign Enforcement for businesses
  that utilize the sidewalk. He also asked staff to provide an update on the Scholl Canyon dump
  closure and also an update on $6M grant that the city received from the state for the Verdugo
  Wash study. Kassakhian stated that $6M for a study seems too much money and suggested
  that the city allocate some of the funds for acquisition of park spaces or find other ways to
  utilize those funds.

  Councilmember Asatryan announced that the West Coast Customs Academy in Burbank is
  offering a free hands-on automotive training program for individuals who are 18-23 years old.
  The Glendale Youth Alliance is looking to integrate this program into their existing offerings.
  The Burbank Adult School has integrated this program in their curriculum as well.
  Councilmember Asatryan asked staff to introduce this program to Glendale Community
  2
   College. More information about this program can be found on the West Coast Customs
  website.

  Councilmember Najarian attended the Independent Cities Association Winter Seminar with
  City Manager Roubik Golanian and Police Chief Manuel Cid. The seminar discussed public
  safety, police recruiting and retention, crisis communication, technology used in policing,
  fentanyl crisis, and civility and chaos at council meetings. Najarian encouraged his colleagues
  to attend these seminars to discuss mutual concerns and build camaraderie with other
  councilmembers and mayors.

  Mayor Brotman spoke about his Japan trip and thanked the Japanese Counsel General for
  arranging the trip. He said that the mayor of our Sister City Higashiosaka, Japan, is interested
  is rekindling the business venture with the City of Glendale that was disrupted ten years ago.

  City Manager Roubik Golanian provided a brief storm update. Councilmember Devine
  commended Public Works staff for working on clearing the roads with debris after the recent
  storms.
